page: Microsoft Azure E104id_v5 is an isolated, memory-optimized virtual machine from the EIDv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 104 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor with 52 physical cores and hyper-threading. The CPU operates at a base speed of 2.8 GHz and includes 48 MB of L3 cache. This server is configured with 672.0 GB of RAM, providing 6.46 GB of memory per core, and includes 3891 GB of local SSD storage.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores placing in the top 25%. Single-core performance is average, as shown by stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core results. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only large block and write large block tests scoring in the top 25%. The processor's cryptographic capabilities are exceptional, with the Passmark CPU encryption test ranking in the top 10%, aided by hardware-accelerated instruction sets like AES and VAES. Database operations and Redis SET operations also demonstrate strong performance in the top 25%. However, without a dedicated GPU, large-scale LLM text generation is a notable bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E104id_v5 offers high resource density, combining massive memory capacity with a substantial local SSD on a dedicated, isolated hypervisor allocation. This makes it highly suitable for enterprise-grade relational databases, large-scale in-memory caching systems like Redis, data warehousing, and heavy multi-threaded compilation tasks. It is less suited for GPU-dependent deep learning or real-time large language model inference.
